summary: Nicolas Revire is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Silpakorn University and completed his doctorate under Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling (~2010–2016). He held a post at Thammasat University (~2008–2017).

Linguist and Tibetologist Nicolas Tournadre studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University and Paris 8 University. He held posts at INALCO (~1992–1995), Paris 8 University (~1995–2004), University of Virginia (~2000–2004), University of Provence (~2004–2011), Aix-Marseille University (~2012), and LACITO.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She taught Heather Stoddard and held academic posts at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1947–1971), École du Louvre (~1957–1976), and INALCO (~1971–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn, Paris, London, and Oxford before becoming Professor für Indisch-orientalische Philologie at the University of Copenhagen in 1845.
Nigel Allan is a scholar of history and archaeology. He succeeded Marianne Winder as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust.

Niharranjan Ray worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Leiden University, later holding posts at Calcutta (~1936–1965) and as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1965–1970).

Nika Jovic specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (~2005–2010), where she was supervised for her MA by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy.

Nikolai Solmsdorf is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard (until ~2014) and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford (2002–2010) under Alexis Sanderson and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2013).

Ninian Smart specialized in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Oxford and Yale, and held posts at the universities of Birmingham and Nottingham (~1961–1967), Lancaster University (1967), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1976–1998).

Indologist Nirajan Kafle earned his doctorate at Leiden University (~2011–2015) under Peter Bisschop. He subsequently worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Leiden University (~2016–2019) and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti worked in Indology and archaeology. After studying at Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD 1924–1926), he held posts at the University of Calcutta (1917), the Archaeological Survey of India (1929–1950), and as Government Epigraphist for India (~1934–1940).

Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious studies and related fields. He has served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University (~1993–2003), and Clinical Professor at the Medical College of Georgia (~2013).

Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a Tibetologist and historian educated at Calcutta and Presidency University. He held posts at Krishnath College, the National Archives of India (~1946–1958), and the University of Calcutta as Centenary Professor of International Relations (1971).
Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (~2013–2015), where he was supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Noa Gal is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford (~1999–2003) under the doctoral supervision of Richard Gombrich.

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (~1999–2003) and was later a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University (~2005–2006).

Noboru Karashima specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held professorships and academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1974), University of Tokyo (~1974–1994), Taisho University (~1994–2008), and Open University of Japan (~1996–2004).
Noboru Kuge is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who was taught by Kyoichiro Mizuno. He held a post as professor at Bukkyo University.
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Mejiro University.
